title: Open and closed restrictions of coefficient-linear extension by zero
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring, with coefficient ring objects $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ and module objects as in [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be a quasi-compact open immersion of schemes and $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ a closed immersion whose image is $X\setminus j(U)$. Use coefficient module pullbacks $g^*=\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_g}\operatorname{mapMod}(g^*_{\Ab})$ [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback] and the coefficient-linear extension by zero $j_!$ [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek]. For every $M\in\Mod_{\Lambda_U}$ there are natural isomorphisms $j^*j_!M\cong M$ and $i^*j_!M\cong0$. No finiteness condition on $\Lambda$ or Noetherian condition on the schemes is required.

source.place: Proof: "On $U_a$ the restriction of $j_!M$ is $M|_{U_a}$, because $j^*j_!\cong\mathrm{id}$. On $X\setminus U$ it is $0$"; isolate the coefficient-category restriction identities.

proof.text: For $T=X,U,Z$, let $B_T$ be the section-ring sheaf of $\Lambda_T$ and let $E_T:\Mod_{\Lambda_T}\simeq\Mod(B_T)$ be the equivalence in [lem-sfb-internal-module-operations-transport]. Its statement gives the coefficient identifications $g^{-1}B_X\cong B_T$ induced by $\alpha_g$ and natural comparisons $c_g:E_Tg^*\cong g^*_{\rm sec}E_X$ for $g=j,i$. It also gives $o:E_Xj_!\cong LE_U$, where $L=j_{!,\rm sec}$ is left adjoint to $R=j^*_{\rm sec}$. These comparisons are for the actual tensor pullbacks and the coefficient-linear extension of the item, not merely the underlying abelian sheaves.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-proetale-identified-open-closed] with coefficient sheaves $B_X,B_Z,B_U$ and the identifications just obtained. The schemes, closed immersion, complementary quasi-compact open immersion, and arbitrary commutative coefficient rings meet exactly its hypotheses. It supplies an additive sectionwise functor $F:\Mod(B_U)\to\Mod(B_X)$ and adjunction $F\dashv R$ with invertible unit $\eta^F:\mathrm{id}\to RF$, together with $i^*_{\rm sec}F(N)\cong0$ for every $N$. There is no Noetherian or coefficient-finiteness hypothesis in this application.

source.place: Tags 09BN (lemma-open-immersion), 09AH (lemma-ses-associated-to-open); module extension by zero: sites-modules.tex Tag 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero). Internal/sectionwise comparison is the cited transport theorem; the composition argument is agent-written.

proof.text: Identify $L$ with $F$ as left adjoints to the same $R$, writing $\eta^L,\varepsilon^L$ and $\eta^F,\varepsilon^F$ for their units and counits. Explicitly, $a_N=\varepsilon^F_{LN}\circ F(\eta^L_N):FN\to LN$ and $b_N=\varepsilon^L_{FN}\circ L(\eta^F_N):LN\to FN$ are natural. Under the $F\dashv R$ Hom bijection, $b_Na_N$ and $\mathrm{id}_{FN}$ both transpose to $\eta^F_N$; under $L\dashv R$, $a_Nb_N$ and $\mathrm{id}_{LN}$ both transpose to $\eta^L_N$, by naturality and the triangle identities. Hence $b:L\cong F$. In particular $o$ gives $\widetilde o:E_Xj_!\cong FE_U$ by composition with $bE_U$. This checks the identity of the extension functors, rather than choosing a different extension with the same name.

proof.text: Compose the natural isomorphisms from the previous steps to obtain $E_U(j^*j_!M)\xrightarrow{c_j}R(E_Xj_!M)\xrightarrow{R(\widetilde o_M)}RF(E_UM)\xrightarrow{(\eta^F_{E_UM})^{-1}}E_UM$. Since $E_U$ is fully faithful, this lifts uniquely to an isomorphism $j^*j_!M\cong M$: lift the displayed map and its inverse by fullness, then use faithfulness to check their two composites are identities. Apply the same faithfulness to each naturality square, giving naturality in $M$.

proof.text: Likewise $E_Z(i^*j_!M)\xrightarrow{c_i}i^*_{\rm sec}(E_Xj_!M)\xrightarrow{i^*_{\rm sec}(\widetilde o_M)}i^*_{\rm sec}F(E_UM)\cong0$. The additive equivalence $E_Z$ sends the zero internal module to a zero sectionwise module. Fullness and faithfulness lift the last composite and its inverse to $i^*j_!M\cong0$, as in Step 4. The maps to and from zero are unique, so this isomorphism is natural in $M$. The argument uses only the hypotheses checked in Step 2, and thus establishes the stated absence of finiteness and Noetherian restrictions.
